# Pelican Engine

Pelican is a single npm package for TypeScript games authored by external coding agents. Install pelican-engine in a separate game workspace; the repository is for engine contributors.

## Discover before choosing an implementation

- Run `npx pelican guide --compact` first, or `guide --goal "让角色跳跃并保存游戏"`, for ranked tasks, exact methods, complete recipes and verification steps. Unrecognized tasks return labelled navigation candidates, not invented support.
- Run `npx pelican capabilities --summary --limit 8` to browse; follow total/truncated/nextOffset. Use `--feature <goal>` for the full limits before implementation.
- Run `npx pelican api --symbol <Type.member>` for an exact method contract.
- Run `npx pelican api --search <goal> --member --limit 8` for compact ranked methods.
- Run `npx pelican recipe --id <id>` for complete source files and dependency requirements.
- Unknown search results are not proof of unsupported behavior. Search aliases and the owning service before implementing a replacement.

## Authoring

- Game workflow: docs/npm/GAME-AUTHOR.md
- Dependencies, lifecycle, geometry and rendering integrations: docs/npm/INTEGRATIONS.md
- Exact generated SDK contract: docs/api/index.json and lib/sdk/index.d.ts in the npm package
- Capability boundaries: docs/CAPABILITIES.md

Ordinary browser-compatible npm algorithms can be used directly. defineGameRuntime declares systems once, allocates validated per-instance JSON state and supplies save hooks. Browser-only libraries initialize in setup/runtime.create; scope.own/listen/cleanup/defer manages cleanup. Low-level versioned snapshot/validateSnapshot/restore remains supported. No game-runtime language model or mandatory AI platform is required.

Use scope.own(resource, release) for ordinary component objects and scope.listen for scoped EventTarget subscriptions. createRuntimeAdapter accepts an explicit owned/borrowed endpoint and send/subscribe/decode callbacks; drain its bounded queue in a fixed-tick system. The external-adapters recipe includes a real module Worker, optional WebSocket and managed rendering-buffer updates. External inputs are not automatically saved or replayed; keep engine resource checks and explicitly resynchronize external protocols on restore.

Use your own functions, classes, modules, generators and rules alongside engine services. Built-in inventory, quest and dialogue services are optional. This is ordinary TypeScript, not an engine-only DSL. Node-only packages belong in build/asset tooling, not browser runtime.

Complete tasks: third-person (movement, grounded jump, follow, save/load), runtime-lifecycle (real npm dependency), external-adapters (Worker/WebSocket), dynamic-resources (bounded cancellable JSON to managed buffers). Concrete adapters createWorkerAdapter/createWebSocketAdapter share the generic ownership contract. Dynamic data is not automatically persisted; loadRuntimeJSON does not implement full model streaming.

Use defineGameRuntime<State, Dependencies> when setup returns instance-local browser/npm objects; synchronous systems receive the typed dependency context as their fifth argument. It is not serialized or implicitly disposed. The npm-component recipe demonstrates this without globals. loadRuntimeBytes uses the same bounded cancellable transport for npm codecs; dynamic-texture demonstrates PNG-to-managed-texture publication. Validate decoded dimensions before allocating; encoded-byte budgets are not decoded-memory budgets.

Development preserves full state for compatible logic-only edits. Changed declarations/assets require explicit restart; a failed candidate keeps the old instance. Inspect iteration diagnostics. Default/low/realtime is raster; explicit high is path, medium/preview is hybrid; capture is unfiltered path. Tracing requires WebGPU. WebGL2 can run default raster. Built-in WebGPU raster adds full-resolution indirect AO; custom postprocess owns presentation. prepare/preparation prewarms at frame boundaries without switching mode or advancing simulation; retained caches consume memory. Query render-quality recipe. No fixed FPS or universal tier performance ordering is guaranteed.

Use managed geometry, PBR textures, compute resources and defineRenderExtension for supported rendering integration. Arbitrary Three.js, TSL, raw GPU or physics objects are not a stable engine integration contract. Report an exact missing capability instead of silently replacing the renderer or reducing the requested game.

Bounded inspect: pelican inspect --summary or --fields summary,rendering. Capture --facts measures final display pixels with evidence, not author intent. pelican verify is a smoke check; --recipe <id> runs shared acceptance for the original template. HTTP reference: docs/npm/HTTP-PROTOCOL.md. Host-accounted tokens are null when unavailable; external AI task success is distinct from prewritten regression.
